mainTopic: Courtyard עירוב problems: a forgetful resident, ביטול רשות on שבת, and when a גוי forbids carrying in a מבוי
overview: This amud begins at the end of רבא's ruling about an inner חצר and an outer חצר that share one עירוב. If someone from the outer חצר forgot to join, the inner חצר is still permitted, because its residents can shut the door. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע asks why a forgetful inner resident cannot simply do ביטול רשות. רבא answers that this fix works only for רבי אליעזר. He ruled like the רבנן, who require giving up rights to every single resident. After a short story about how רב חסדא and רב ששת were in awe of each other, רב חסדא asks רב ששת two questions. The first is about two houses that גוים fenced in on שבת, and רב ששת rules אין מבטלין. The second is about a גוי in a shared courtyard who died on שבת. There רב ששת allows ביטול, while רב המנונא forbids it. Then שמואל rules that a גוי whose courtyard has its own opening to a valley does not forbid the מבוי, because he prefers his private entrance. The גמרא asks what happens if that opening leads to a קרפף instead, and רב נחמן בר אמי's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When someone from the outer courtyard forgets, the inner courtyard is still permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his ruling: if a resident of the outer חצר did not join the עירוב, the inner חצר stays permitted, but the outer חצר is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one resident of the outer courtyard forgot and did not join the עירוב, the inner courtyard is certainly permitted, because its residents can close the door and use their own courtyard. But the outer courtyard is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבא's ruling about two connected courtyards. This is the case where the person who forgot lives in the outer חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The residents of the inner חצר can simply shut the door between the courtyards and use their own courtyard by themselves, so the outer person's mistake does not affect them. The outer חצר is still forbidden, because the resident who forgot lives there and did not join. This is the opposite of the earlier case, where a forgetful inner resident made both courtyards forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Made or joined an עירוב, the shared food that lets residents carry together on שבת
The inner courtyard, whose only way out is through the outer one
The outer courtyard, which opens to the street
Because it can close the door
Certainly, without question

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. When someone from the OUTER חצר forgets, only the outer one is forbidden. When someone from the INNER חצר forgets, both are forbidden, because the inner residents have a right to walk through the outer חצר.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁכַח אֶחָד מִן הַחִיצוֹנָה וְלֹא עֵירַב —
phrases.english: If one resident of the outer courtyard forgot and did not join the eruv —
the inner courtyard is certainly permitted,
because it can close the door and use its own courtyard,
phrases.notes: The inner residents lock the connecting door and cut themselves off from the outer courtyard.

phrases.english: but the outer courtyard is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁכַח אֶחָד מִן הַחִיצוֹנָה וְלֹא עֵירַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's ruling on the previous amud, where a forgetful inner resident made both courtyards forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If an outer resident forgets the עירוב, the inner חצר is permitted because it can close itself off, and the outer חצר is forbidden.

steps.title: Why can't the forgetful inner resident simply give up his rights?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע asks רבא: when an inner resident forgets, why are both courtyards forbidden? He could do ביטול רשות to his inner neighbors, and then the outer חצר would be permitted together with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said to רבא: When someone from the inner courtyard forgot and did not join the עירוב, why are both courtyards forbidden? Let him give up his rights to the other inner residents. Then the outer courtyard, which joined with them, would become permitted along with them!
steps.whatsHappening: A student challenges רבא's earlier ruling that a forgetful inner resident forbids both courtyards. He suggests an easy fix: ביטול רשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the forgetful person gives up his rights, he no longer counts as a resident, so he cannot forbid anything. The other inner residents already share an עירוב with the outer courtyard. So, the challenger argues, everyone should be able to carry, and there is no reason for both courtyards to stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him give up (his rights), meaning ביטול רשות
A resident of the inner courtyard
Why?
And let it become permitted
Together with them

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי שָׁכַח אֶחָד מִן הַפְּנִימִית וְלֹא עֵירַב
phrases.english: And when one resident of the inner courtyard forgot and did not join the eruv,
why are both courtyards forbidden?
Let the inner resident renounce his rights to the other inner residents,
and let the outer courtyard come and be permitted together with them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the other half of רבא's ruling, the case where an inner resident forgot.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a forgetful inner resident makes both courtyards forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ביטול רשות to the inner neighbors should remove the problem entirely, so the outer חצר, which shares an עירוב with the inner one, should be permitted too.

steps.title: Your fix works only for רבי אליעזר; I ruled like the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the suggestion follows רבי אליעזר, who says giving up rights to one person is enough. רבא ruled like the רבנן, who require giving up rights to every resident. That would include the outer residents, and rights cannot be given up from one חצר to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion are you following? רבי אליעזר's, who says a person does not need to give up his rights to each and every resident? When I spoke, I was following the רבנן, who say a person must give up his rights to each and every resident!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his ruling. He explains that the suggested fix depends on a מחלוקת, and his ruling follows the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, the forgetful person would have to give up his rights to every member of the shared עירוב, including the people in the outer חצר. But ביטול רשות does not work from one courtyard to another. So the fix fails and both courtyards stay forbidden. According to רבי אליעזר, giving up rights to the inner neighbors alone would be enough, and the challenge would be correct.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (asks which opinion an idea follows)
A תנא who holds that ביטול רשות to one person is enough
To each and every one
When I said it, I meant...
The Sages, the majority opinion

steps.whatToRemember: Under the רבנן, ביטול רשות must be given to every single resident who shares the עירוב. Because rights cannot be given up across courtyards, a forgetful inner resident leaves both courtyards forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not deny that ביטול רשות exists here. He explains that it cannot reach the outer residents, because rights are not given up from one חצר to another. רבא does not say this rule out loud, but the גמרא names it soon after (step 6: אין ביטול רשות מחצר לחצר).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one ruling can depend on a basic מחלוקת. The disagreement over whether ביטול רשות goes to everyone or to one person decides the practical result.

phrases.english: According to whom? According to Rabbi Eliezer,
who said: One does not need to renounce his rights
to each and every resident?
When I spoke, it was according to the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרִי: צָרִיךְ לְבַטֵּל לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד!
phrases.english: who say: One must renounce his rights to each and every resident!
phrases.notes: That would include the outer residents, which cannot be done between courtyards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 by tying it to a מחלוקת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to one side of a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ביטול רשות to the inner neighbors alone would permit both courtyards.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under the רבנן, ביטול רשות must go to every resident, including the outer ones. That is impossible across courtyards, so both courtyards stay forbidden.

steps.title: How רב חסדא and רב ששת were each in awe of the other
steps.stepSummary: A short story: when רב חסדא and רב ששת met, רב חסדא's lips trembled at רב ששת's vast knowledge of sources, and רב ששת's whole body shook at רב חסדא's sharp reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב חסדא and רב ששת met each other, רב חסדא's lips would tremble because of רב ששת's knowledge of the sources. And רב ששת's whole body would tremble because of רב חסדא's sharp reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the legal discussion to tell a short story about two great אמוראים. It sets up the next part of the סוגיא, where the two of them discuss these courtyard laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each scholar was strong in a different way. רב ששת knew the sources, the ברייתות, by heart. רב חסדא was brilliant at sharp analysis, called פלפול. Each respected the other's strength deeply.

keyTerms.meaning: They would meet
His lips would tremble
Memorized teachings, such as ברייתות (knowledge of sources)
His sharp analytical reasoning

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that both broad knowledge of sources and sharp reasoning are valued in learning. The story also introduces the exchange between these two scholars that follows.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת כִּי פָּגְעִי בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי —
phrases.english: When Rav Chisda and Rav Sheshet would meet each other —
Rav Chisda's lips would tremble
because of Rav Sheshet's knowledge of the sources,
and Rav Sheshet's entire body would tremble
because of Rav Chisda's sharp reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת כִּי פָּגְעִי בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the legal back-and-forth to a story that introduces the next discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not a legal ruling. The story describes the mutual awe between רב חסדא, known for sharp reasoning, and רב ששת, known for knowledge of sources.

steps.title: רב חסדא's question: two houses enclosed on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks רב ששת about two houses across a public street that גוים fenced in on שבת. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא asked רב ששת: There are two houses on two sides of a public street. Non-Jews came and put a wall around them on שבת. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a question that רב חסדא asked רב ששת. It describes a new case and asks what the law is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before שבת, the public street between the houses blocked any עירוב. On שבת the wall turned the whole area into one private domain, so carrying is allowed by Torah law. The open question is about the rabbinic level: can one owner give up his rights so the other may carry?

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him (a formal question to a teacher or colleague)
Public domain (a public street or area)
Partition or wall
What is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the wall works by Torah law. It does. The question is only whether ביטול רשות can solve the rabbinic problem.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda asked of Rav Sheshet:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי בָתִּים מִשְּׁנֵי צִידֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
phrases.english: Two houses on two sides of a public domain
and non-Jews came and surrounded them with a partition on Shabbat,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the story of רב חסדא and רב ששת with an actual question between them, and builds on the topic of ביטול רשות from steps 2-3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can ביטול רשות permit carrying between two houses that became one enclosed area only on שבת?

steps.title: No question for the view that forbids giving up rights between courtyards
steps.stepSummary: For the view that says אין ביטול רשות מחצר לחצר, the answer is obvious: no. This follows by a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Take the view that says you cannot give up rights from one חצר to another. For that view there is no question. Think about two neighboring courtyards: they could have made an עירוב yesterday if they wanted, and still you say there is no giving up rights. Here they could not have made an עירוב yesterday at all. Isn't it even more obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the question. It shows that under one opinion the question does not even start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two neighboring courtyards could have joined with an עירוב before שבת, yet this view still forbids ביטול רשות between them. The two houses could never have joined before שבת. So by a קל וחומר, ביטול רשות surely does not help them either.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who said
Giving up one's rights to a shared area so others may carry
From one courtyard to another
You have no question
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: According to the one who said
there is no giving up of rights from courtyard to courtyard,
you have no question.
Now, where if they had wanted to make an eruv yesterday
they could have made an eruv,
you say 'there is no giving up of rights from courtyard to courtyard,'
then here, where if they had wanted to make an eruv yesterday
they could not have made an eruv,
is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין בִּיטּוּל רְשׁוּת מֵחָצֵר לְחָצֵר לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב חסדא's question by setting aside one opinion.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out the question for the view that forbids ביטול רשות between courtyards.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under that view the answer is obvious by קל וחומר, so there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: The real question: does it matter that no עירוב was possible before שבת?
steps.stepSummary: For the view that allows ביטול רשות between courtyards, the question has two sides. Maybe ביטול works only where an עירוב was possible yesterday. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question is real according to the view that you can give up rights from one חצר to another. Maybe there, where they could have made an עירוב yesterday, they can also give up rights. But here, where they could not have made an עירוב yesterday, they also cannot give up rights. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the real question and lays out both sides of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: ביטול רשות works only as a stand-in for an עירוב that was possible before שבת. Here it was never possible, so ביטול does not work. Side two: what matters is the situation now, when the area is enclosed, so the past does not matter and ביטול works.

keyTerms.meaning: Where you do have a question
To make an עירוב from yesterday (before שבת)
To give up rights
Or perhaps there is no difference

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key idea: ביטול רשות may depend on whether an עירוב could have been made before שבת.

phrases.english: Where you have a question is
according to the one who said
'there is giving up of rights from courtyard to courtyard.'
There, where if they had wanted to make an eruv yesterday
they could have made an eruv,
he can also give up rights;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּלָא מָצוּ מְעָרְבִי מֵאֶתְמוֹל —
phrases.english: but here, where they could not have made an eruv yesterday,
he also cannot give up rights.
Or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ בִּיטּוּל רְשׁוּת מֵחָצֵר לְחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting aside one view, the גמרא states the real question under the other view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does ביטול רשות require that an עירוב could have been made before שבת?

steps.title: רב ששת answers: one may not give up rights
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules אין מבטלין: ביטול רשות does not work in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to him: One may not give up rights.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers רב חסדא's question. ביטול רשות does not help here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת takes the first side. ביטול רשות works only where an עירוב was possible before שבת. These houses were split by a public street before שבת, so ביטול cannot permit carrying between them, even though the area is now enclosed.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not give up rights

steps.whatToRemember: Even for the view that allows ביטול רשות between courtyards, it does not work where no עירוב was possible before שבת, such as houses that were enclosed only on שבת.

phrases.english: He said to him:
One may not give up rights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question laid out in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אין מבטלין: ביטול רשות does not work where no עירוב was possible before שבת.

steps.title: What if the non-Jewish neighbor dies on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks about two Jews and a גוי sharing a courtyard. Nothing was arranged before שבת, and the גוי died on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the non-Jew died on שבת, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא asks רב ששת a second question. Two Jews share a courtyard with a גוי, and the גוי dies on שבת. Can the Jews now fix the courtyard so carrying is allowed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the גוי was alive, his presence forbade carrying, and no one rented his rights before שבת. Now that he is dead, he no longer forbids anything. The question is whether one Jew may now do ביטול רשות for the other, even though this was impossible when שבת began.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law? (opens a question)
A non-Jew

phrases.english: If the non-Jew died on Shabbat, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The case: two Jews and a non-Jew share one courtyard, and his rights were not rented before שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question from רב חסדא to רב ששת, built like the first one about the houses that גוים fenced in.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ביטול רשות works when the גוי who forbade carrying dies on שבת.

steps.title: For those who allow renting on שבת, there is no question
steps.stepSummary: Some hold you may rent from a גוי on שבת. Under that view, ביטול alone is surely allowed, so the question disappears.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the view that we may rent on שבת, you have no question. If we may do two actions, is it even a question that we may do one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the question. It says that under one opinion, there is nothing to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the view that one may rent from a גוי on שבת, the Jews would rent his rights and then also do ביטול. That is two actions done on שבת. If two actions are allowed, then one action alone (just ביטול, after the גוי died) is surely allowed. This is a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
We may rent (the גוי's rights in the courtyard)
Two (actions)
Is one even a question? (surely it is allowed)

phrases.english: According to the one who says we may rent (from a gentile on Shabbat),
you should have no question:
now, if we may do two actions,
is one action even a question?!
phrases.notes: Just renouncing, since the gentile is gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר שׂוֹכְרִין לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Removes one opinion from the question, so we can see exactly where the doubt lies.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The question is rejected only for the view that allows renting on שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under that view the answer follows from a קל וחומר: if two actions are allowed, one action surely is.

steps.title: The real question: for those who forbid renting on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Under the view that forbids renting on שבת, the question has two sides. Maybe only two actions are forbidden. Or maybe even one action is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is according to the view that we may not rent on שבת. Is it only two actions that we may not do, but one action we may do? Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the real doubt. It lays out both sides of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: renting is forbidden only because it means doing two actions on שבת, so plain ביטול (one action) is fine. Side two: the number of actions does not matter. The courtyard was already forbidden when שבת began, because no one rented from the גוי beforehand, so even one action does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, where you should ask
We may not rent (on שבת)
Or perhaps
There is no difference

phrases.english: Rather, where you should ask
is according to the one who says we may not rent.
Is it two actions that we do not do,
but one action we do?
Or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין שׂוֹכְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting one view aside, the גמרא states the real two-sided question under the other view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the ban on renting about the number of actions (two), or does it apply even to a single act of ביטול?

steps.title: רב ששת: I allow renouncing, רב המנונא does not
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that he holds מבטלין, but he reports that רב המנונא holds אין מבטלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I say we may renounce rights, and רב המנונא said we may not renounce rights.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers רב חסדא. He gives his own view and also reports a differing view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת holds that one Jew may do ביטול רשות for the other after the גוי dies. In this case only one action is needed. רב המנונא disagrees and forbids it. Notice that in the earlier case (step 8), רב ששת ruled אין מבטלין, but here he allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: We may renounce (rights in the courtyard)
An אמורא who disagrees with רב ששת here

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two rulings. In the fenced-houses case (step 8), רב ששת said אין מבטלין. In this case, where the גוי died, he says מבטלין.

phrases.english: He (Rav Sheshet) said to him: I say we may renounce rights,
and Hamnuna said we may not renounce rights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided question from step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ששת: ביטול רשות is allowed after the גוי dies. רב המנונא: it is not allowed.

steps.title: A non-Jew with his own opening to a valley does not forbid the alley
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a גוי whose courtyard has a 4x4 opening to a valley does not forbid carrying in the alley. This is true even if he uses the alley heavily.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A גוי who has an opening of four by four טפחים that opens to a valley does not forbid the residents of the alley from carrying. This is so even if he brings camels and wagons in and out through the alley all day long.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ruling from שמואל. It is about when a גוי counts as a resident of a shared alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a גוי living on the alley forbids carrying there until his rights are rented. But if his courtyard has its own opening of at least four by four טפחים to an open valley, that opening is treated as his real entrance. So he is not counted as part of the alley, no matter how much he actually uses it.

keyTerms.meaning: An opening or doorway
Four by four טפחים (the minimum size of a real opening)
A valley or open field
An alley that several courtyards open into
Forbids (carrying for others)

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that an opening of at least four by four טפחים is enough to make it the גוי's main entrance. What counts is the legal opening, not how much he actually uses the alley.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
a gentile who has an opening
of four by four handbreadths
that opens to a valley,
even if he brings in and takes out
camels and wagons
the entire day by way of the alleyway,
does not forbid (carrying) for the residents of the alleyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל גּוֹי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ פֶּתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on a related topic: when a גוי's presence forbids carrying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי with a 4x4 opening to a valley does not forbid the alley residents, even if he uses the alley constantly.

steps.title: Why does the valley opening count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind שמואל's ruling about the גוי with an opening to a valley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל ruled that the גוי does not forbid the מבוי, even though he uses it a lot. This short question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling sounds surprising. The גוי walks through the מבוי often, so we might expect him to count as a resident there. The גמרא wants to know what makes the small valley opening so important.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Asking for the logic behind שמואל's ruling from Step 13.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind שמואל's ruling in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a 4x4 opening to a valley stops the גוי from forbidding the מבוי, even when he uses the מבוי heavily.

steps.title: His private entrance is the one he prefers
steps.stepSummary: The גוי prefers the entrance that belongs only to him, so that opening counts as his main entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: An entrance that is his alone is the one he is happy with.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the גוי treats his private valley opening as his real entrance. So he is not seen as a resident of the מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the valley opening is small, it belongs to him alone, and nobody shares it. He uses the מבוי only when it is handy. Because his main entrance is somewhere else, he does not forbid the Jews in the מבוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Entrance, opening
Set aside for him alone, private to him
He is comfortable with it, he prefers it

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that a person's main entrance is the one he prefers, is what makes the next question possible: does a קרפף opening count as a preferred entrance too?

phrases.english: With an entrance that is exclusively his,
phrases.notes: The valley opening belongs only to the גוי.

phrases.english: with that one he is content.
phrases.notes: He views it as his main entrance, even though it is small.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפִיתְחָא דִּמְיַחַד לֵיהּ בְּהָהוּא נִיחָא לֵיהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A private entrance is the one a person prefers, so the valley opening is the גוי's main entrance. The מבוי is only a side route for him.

steps.title: What if the opening leads to an enclosure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the גוי's extra opening leads into a קרפף instead of a valley, does the same rule apply?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if it opens into an enclosure, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question based on the reason it just gave. It asks what happens if the גוי's private opening leads into a קרפף (an enclosed area) and not into a valley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that a private opening counts as the main entrance because the גוי prefers it. A קרפף is a different kind of place from an open valley. So we are not sure whether the גוי would still treat that opening as his real entrance.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים)
An enclosed area outside the house, such as a fenced storage yard
What is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up a קרפף with a valley. A valley (בקעה) is open land, while a קרפף is fenced in. The whole question is whether this difference matters.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
phrases.notes: Standard opening for a real question in the בית מדרש.

phrases.english: If it opens into an enclosure, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The גוי's courtyard opens to the מבוי and also to a קרפף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reason in Step 15 and tests it on a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an opening to a קרפף counts as the גוי's preferred main entrance, like an opening to a valley, so that he does not forbid the מבוי.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר אמי begins to answer from a tradition
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר אמי starts to answer the question by quoting what he received from his teachers. The answer itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר אמי said, quoting the tradition of his teachers:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces the answer to the קרפף question. This line only sets up the answer, and the actual ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר אמי does not answer from his own reasoning. He quotes a tradition he learned from the בית מדרש. That gives the answer the weight of a received teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who answers the question
In the name of the learning, meaning a tradition received from his teachers

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Ami said
phrases.notes: Attribution for the answer that follows.

phrases.english: citing the tradition of his teachers:
phrases.notes: The content of the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאוּלְפָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the attribution appears here. The ruling itself, based on a received tradition, continues on the next amud.
